### Describe the bug

I'm reporting [this issue from Cartopy](https://github.com/SciTools/cartopy/issues/2722) upstream as I can't see what exactly is going wrong. The attached code is a distilled version of https://github.com/SciTools/cartopy/blob/main/lib/cartopy/trace.pyx When I run `cythonize` on the code, it results in the following compile error somewhere in Cython internals:
```
$ CYTHON_FORCE_REGEN=1 ./cythonize.py trace.pyx 
[1/1] Cythonizing /home/elliott/code/cython/trace.pyx

Error compiling Cython file:
------------------------------------------------------------
...
    cdef cpp_list[X].const_iterator iter = v.begin()

    while iter != v.end():
        item = cython.operator.dereference(iter)
        Py_INCREF(item)
        __Pyx_PyList_SET_ITEM(o, i, item)
                              ^
------------------------------------------------------------
list.to_py:145:30: Cannot convert 'list[T]' to Python object

Error compiling Cython file:
------------------------------------------------------------
...
        Py_INCREF(item)
        __Pyx_PyList_SET_ITEM(o, i, item)
        cython.operator.preincrement(iter)
        i += 1

    return o
           ^
------------------------------------------------------------
list.to_py:149:11: Cannot convert 'list[T]' to Python object
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/elliott/code/cython/./cythonize.py", line 9, in <module>
    main()
    ~~~~^^
  File "/home/elliott/code/cython/Cython/Build/Cythonize.py", line 324, in main
    ext_modules_by_basedir = _cython_compile_files(all_paths, options)
  File "/home/elliott/code/cython/Cython/Build/Cythonize.py", line 51, in _cython_compile_files
    ext_modules = cythonize(
        paths,
    ...<8 lines>...
        language=options.language,
        **options.options)
  File "/home/elliott/code/cython/Cython/Build/Dependencies.py", line 1153, in cythonize
    cythonize_one(*args)
    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^
  File "/home/elliott/code/cython/Cython/Build/Dependencies.py", line 1264, in cythonize_one
    raise CompileError(None, pyx_file)
Cython.Compiler.Errors.CompileError: /home/elliott/code/cython/trace.pyx
```

The crash does not point to anything in the original code, but if I remove the class attribute, then it builds fine.

If I build with 3.2.9, then it also is fine. AFAICT, with that version, the `lines` attribute is not exposed in any way to Python, so I'm not sure what is causing a `PyList_SET_ITEM` call:
```python
>>> from cartopy.trace import LineAccumulator
>>> dir(LineAccumulator)
['__class__', '__delattr__', '__dir__', '__doc__', '__eq__', '__format__', '__ge__', '__getattribute__', '__getstate__', '__gt__', '__hash__', '__init__', '__init_subclass__', '__le__', '__lt__', '__ne__', '__new__', '__pyx_vtable__', '__reduce__', '__reduce_ex__', '__repr__', '__setattr__', '__setstate__', '__sizeof__', '__str__', '__subclasshook__']
>>> la = LineAccumulator()
>>> dir(la)
['__class__', '__delattr__', '__dir__', '__doc__', '__eq__', '__format__', '__ge__', '__getattribute__', '__getstate__', '__gt__', '__hash__', '__init__', '__init_subclass__', '__le__', '__lt__', '__ne__', '__new__', '__pyx_vtable__', '__reduce__', '__reduce_ex__', '__repr__', '__setattr__', '__setstate__', '__sizeof__', '__str__', '__subclasshook__']
```

### Code to reproduce the behaviour:

```cython
# distutils: language = c++

from libcpp.list cimport list

cdef class LineAccumulator:
    cdef list[double] lines
```


### Expected behaviour

Compile works, as it does with 3.2.9.

### OS

Fedora 44

### Python version

3.14.6

### Cython version

6d669bf6e19bc497508f092fd3129d17a1573f07

### Additional context

A bisect from 3.2.9 to 3.3.0 points to 6d669bf6e19bc497508f092fd3129d17a1573f07 but I'm uncertain how that caused the problem.

comment_data.body:
Of course, as usually happens, I figured out a workaround after filing the bug. It appears that the auto-pickling code is the cause of this, as if I explicitly disable it, then it will compile:
```cython
# distutils: language = c++

cimport cython
from libcpp.list cimport list

@cython.auto_pickle(False)
cdef class LineAccumulator:
    cdef list[double] lines
```

However, with 3.2.9, pickling _did_ work, so it's not that it's accidentally trying to enable it in 3.3.0:
```python
>>> from cartopy.trace import LineAccumulator
>>> la = LineAccumulator()
>>> import pickle
>>> pickle.dumps(la)
b'\x80\x05\x95Z\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x8c\rcartopy.trace\x94\x8c\x1e__pyx_unpickle_LineAccumulator\x94\x93\x94h\x00\x8c\x0fLineAccumulator\x94\x93\x94J\xc3D\xea\x05]\x94]\x94a\x85\x94\x87\x94R\x94.'
>>> pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(la))
<cartopy.trace.LineAccumulator object at 0x7f694794ae50>
>>> 
```
I also met this bug in sagemath

This bisects to 6d669bf6e19bc497508f092fd3129d17a1573f07

I can be fixed by changing

https://github.com/cython/cython/blob/5ba382cf4122d2d5143c512adc842db4b7c6d15e/Cython/Utility/CppConvert.pyx#L127

to

```
object PyList_New(Py_ssize_t size)
```

Not immediately sure why though - it'd be nice to know that there wasn't a more dramatic problem.

Writing the usercode as

```
# distutils: language = c++

from libcpp.list cimport list as cpp_list

cdef class LineAccumulator:
    cdef cpp_list[double] lines
```

also fixes it, so I think it's just using the C++ `list` from the global scope rather than Python list. That feels dodgy, because even with my proposed fix you can do:

```
from libcpp.list cimport list as object
```

and once again it's broken...

Last comment for now: I suspect the offending line of https://github.com/cython/cython/commit/6d669bf6e19bc497508f092fd3129d17a1573f07 is

line 4640
```
                outer_module_scope=env.global_scope(),
```

We're having this issue as well in [UXarray](https://github.com/UXARRAY/uxarray), which led me to create the ticket mentioned above. Here's a link to our logs for more context:

[https://github.com/UXARRAY/uxarray/actions/runs/32796077701/job/97647544728#step:5:375](https://github.com/UXARRAY/uxarray/actions/runs/32796077701/job/97647544728#step:5:375)

Our upstream CI build is failing on the same file as @QuLogic mentioned above, which wasn't anything new until cython 3.3.0. 

Thanks @QuLogic for making a ticket here! Hope we can figure out the right solution!

> `outer_module_scope=env.global_scope(),`

Hmm, right. That line has more effects than intended. It's definitely not intended to look up types from the module scope. I'll look into it.

Hmm, interesting. The following C++ test fails when `cpp_locals=True` (automatically tested):
```cython
from libcpp.list cimport list

cdef class LineAccumulator:
    """
    >>> la = LineAccumulator()
    >>> la.get_lines()
    [5.0]

    >>> import pickle
    >>> la2 = pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(la))
    >>> la2.get_lines()
    [5.0]
    """
    cdef list[double] lines

    def __init__(self):
        self.lines.push_back(5.0)

    def get_lines(self):
        return self.lines
```
It says `AttributeError: C++ attribute 'lines' is not initialized` in the call to `__init__()`. @da-woods, is that intended? Isn't `cpp_locals` only meant for variables?

I think it was intended - the aim was for c++ types to behave more like Python types generally. If it was a Python list then you'd have to initialize it so the same should apply here. 

Assuming that this is for a test then theres a tag to disable it for cpp_locals and I don't feel bad about using the tag just because not all code should work for both.

> I think it was intended

I added a test and documentation in https://github.com/cython/cython/pull/7950
It's really not obvious otherwise that this is impacted and how to deal with it.
